Q6. A vanilla VAE uses a fully connected layer from 64x64x3 to 512. A convolutional
VAE first reduces the image to 8x8x64 and then uses the same 512-dimensional fully
connected layer. Calculate weights and the reduction.
Answer. First, flatten the image.
Input size = 64 × 64 × 3 = 12,288
Wvanilla = 12,288 × 512 = 6,291,456
For the convolutional representation:
Feature size = 8 × 8 × 64 = 4,096
Wconv = 4,096 × 512 = 2,097,152
Reduction:
Reduction = 6,291,456 − 2,097,152 = 4,194,304 weights
Percentage reduction =
4,194,304
6,291,456
× 100 ≈ 66.67%
Thus the convolutional approach uses about one-third as many weights in this fully connected stage.
The main reason convolutional architectures are preferable for images is even broader: convolutions
exploit locality and weight sharing before the final dense layer, so they can reduce both parameter
count and unnecessary dependence on exact pixel positions.
